messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of about 10 kPa (≈ 0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  
This is a slight depression compared with the standard 0 °C at 1 atm, reflecting the fact that lower pressure reduces the temperature at which the solid and liquid phases of water are in equilibrium.
